Subject: MedOcean — Dedicated GPU isolation & scaling recap

Hi Anya / Marcus — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick written recap so we have the same checklist and owners. I tried to keep this tight with clear next steps.

Summary of pain and goals
- Pain: intermittent tail latency spikes during batch export runs and concerns about PHI isolation across models (inference + embedding pipelines).
- Goal: a dedicated, isolated GPU pool for production inference with predictable latency and an ops playbook that allows scheduled burst capacity for nightly aggregation jobs.

Sizing/throughput we discussed
- Peak online inference: ~120 concurrent requests per second (short prompts ~<512 tokens) during daytime peak.
- Baseline steady-state: 25–35 rps.
- Nightly batch/aggregation: up to 600k tokens/minute for a 2–3 hour window; desire for burst policy rather than permanent overprovisioning.

Isolation & compliance needs
- Tenant isolation (single-tenant pool) for PHI workloads; KMS-managed keying; audit logs retained 1 year.
- SOC 2 evidence required for procurement (we have SOC 2 Type II report and can provide the control matrix).

SLA / targets we talked about
- Availability target requested by MedOcean: 99.95% for dedicated pool.
- Latency target (p95): <300ms for completion requests under 512 tokens; fallback to quantized variant if peak sustained >90% utilization.

Operational/tech notes
- Autoscaling: prefer scheduled burst windows + reactive buffer-based scaling.
- KV/prefix caching for chat use-cases to reduce token spend and lower latency for repeated contexts.
- Suggest starting on a 4-GPU reserved pool (A100 equivalent) with the option to add 2-GPU burst slots for nightly jobs.

Risks and open questions
- Network egress policy for on-prem vs VPC deployment (Marcus to confirm whether public egress is acceptable).
- Procurement timeline: PO approval window and whether a master services agreement is needed.
- Any hard requirements on encryption-at-rest beyond KMS?

Next steps / owners
- MedOcean: confirm procurement contact, whether MSA is required, and finalize retention requirement (Marcus) — due Thu 10/7.
- Redwood (Evelyn/Ben): send sizing map + preliminary SLA draft and a short ops-runbook for the proposed pump-and-burst pattern (attachments) — due Tue 10/5.
- Technical deep-dive session if needed: schedule with Priyom and your infra team next week.

Attachments included: high-level Mutual Action Plan (MedOcean_MAP_v1.pdf) and draft SLA (MedOcean_SLA_Draft.docx) for initial review.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with calendar invites once you confirm the procurement contact.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
